title: YAG laser after cataract surgery
what: Some time after cataract surgery, a cloudy film can form behind the artificial lens. The laser opens a small window in it, and vision becomes clear again.
why: When vision becomes cloudy again after cataract surgery. This happens because of the film behind the lens.
duration: the procedure itself usually takes 5 to 10 minutes; vision often improves the same day or the next

prepare.title: Getting there
prepare.text: The pupil is usually widened, so you cannot drive afterward.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop your regular drops or medicines on your own. Ask your doctor.

steps: The pupil is widened and the eye numbed with drops
You sit at the machine and rest your chin on a stand
Sometimes a lens is placed on your eye
The doctor gives a series of short laser pulses
You hear clicks and see flashes
Afterward, your eye pressure is checked
feel: Afterward, floaters in your vision. They usually lessen in a few days
after: Vision may be blurry for a few hours from the drops
Use eye drops afterward as your doctor prescribes
Come for a checkup when your doctor says
red_flags: Severe eye pain, nausea, or rainbow rings around lights: see an eye doctor urgently
Sudden flashes, many new floaters, or a curtain over the eye: see an eye doctor urgently

faq.a: No. The film behind the artificial lens has gone cloudy. The laser clears it.

faq.q: Will it need to be repeated?
faq.a: Usually not. The film rarely comes back.

reminders.text: YAG laser tomorrow. Bring sunglasses and arrange a ride home.
